items.caption: About half of Earth's oxygen is made in the ocean, by phytoplankton too small to see. One microbe, Prochlorococcus, makes up to a fifth of the oxygen in the whole living world (NOAA). Images: USGS/NASA Landsat, NASA MODIS, NOAA, Apollo 17 (NASA); Prochlorococcus: L. Thompson & N. Watson (MIT).

items.caption: A day on Venus is longer than its year: 243 Earth days to spin once, only 225 to go around the Sun. And it spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west. Images: NASA/JPL-Caltech, NASA/JPL, NASA/SDO, NASA Goddard SVS, NASA/Bill Ingalls. Surface view: reconstruction from Magellan radar.
